name: Vernonia

project_scope.selection_mode: B089 hybrid anchor + B161 strict parent review
project_scope.note: Current learner comparison set contains both canonical parents, Vernonia baldwinii and V. lindheimeri, plus canonical natural hybrid V. × guadalupensis. Plain V. guadalupensis remains a represented source alias of the hybrid concept.

priority: intermediate characters in the natural hybrid
study_strategy.warning: Do not force intermediate plants into either parent. Vernonia × guadalupensis is an accepted natural hybrid between V. baldwinii and V. lindheimeri. V. baldwinii is the much broader-leaved parent; V. lindheimeri has very narrow linear, strongly revolute leaves densely woolly beneath. Mature flowering material and nearby parent populations are important.

quick_comparison: V. baldwinii — broad-leaved parent endpoint: robust ironweed with much broader ovate to lance-ovate leaves; lower surfaces hairy/tomentose.
V. lindheimeri — narrow-leaved parent endpoint: linear cauline leaves about 5–8 cm × 2–4 mm, strongly revolute margins, densely sericeo-tomentose beneath and usually glabrate above.
V. × guadalupensis — accepted natural hybrid; intermediate leaf width, margin roll and indumentum can bridge the parents, so do not force an intermediate plant into either parent.

visual_comparison_plan.primary_teaching_plate: Three-column V. baldwinii | V. × guadalupensis | V. lindheimeri comparison using matched views and the same scale.
matched_views: whole mature mid-stem leaf at same scale
whole flowering habit / terminal head array
annotation_rules: mark blade width and length axes on all three leaves
arrow to revolute margins where present
label upper versus lower leaf surfaces
keep flower color secondary; the lesson is leaf proportion + margin roll + indumentum
visually bracket the hybrid as an intermediate zone rather than drawing a false hard boundary
